newsitem.title: RUSSIA: AGROKHLEB - Low Russia barley crop won't spur import.
newsitem.headline: AGROKHLEB - Low Russia barley crop won't spur import.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from the Agrokhleb Report, published by SovEcon Ltd, an independent research organisation specialising in agricultural production and trade in the former Soviet Union.
LOW RUSSIAN BARLEY CROP WON'T SPUR BIG IMPORTS
MOSCOW, Feb 3 - Russia's barley output in 1996 was flat on 1995's low level.
Production continued to be significantly below the 1991-95 annual average in all the main producing areas, except for the Bashkortostan Republic.
The Northern Caucasus and Central-Chernozem (Black Earth) region, the major barley surplus areas, experienced a second consecutive crop failure.
As a result, Russia's barley exports are expected to be insignificant in 1996/97.
However, barley imports are unlikely to increase in 1996/97, because continued downsizing of Russia's livestock sector will cut annual demand for feeds by five to seven percent.
Increased feed wheat production has offset the decline in barley production.
In sum, Russia remains a net barley importer, but import prospects are slim.
